items.title: UMass football collapses after a 19-point lead against Akron
items.summary: With two games left in the college football regular season, the Massachusetts football team entered Wednesday night’s matchup against Akron needing two more victories to secure bowl-game eligibility. items.title: Akron Comes Back to Edge The Minutemen, 34-33
items.summary: The University of Massachusetts football team jumped out to a 26-7 late first-half lead, but Akron came back to defeat the Minutemen 34-33 on Wednesday evening at McGuirk Alumni Stadium (6,698).

items.title: UMass shut out by Toledo in 24-0 loss
items.summary: The Massachusetts football team struggled to find an answer against Toledo’s physical defense, suffering a 24-0 shutout at the Glass Bowl on Wednesday night. The Minutemen (5-5, 2-4 Mid-American Conference) were held scoreless for the first time this season, while the Rockets (8-2, 5-1 MAC) earned their first in-conference shutout win since 2000. items.title: UMass Football Falls At Toledo On Wednesday Night
items.summary: TOLEDO, Ohio – The University of Massachusetts football team dropped a 24-0 decision at Toledo on Wednesday night at the Glass Bowl (19,137).

items.title: Dotsey, Eskit And Watson III Selected As UMass Student-Athletes of the Week
items.summary: AMHERST, Mass. – Three student-athletes earned this week's UMass Student-Athletes of the Week, presented by UMassFive College Credit Union. Caroline Dotsey from women's basketball, Ethan Eskit from hockey, and William "Pop" Watson III from football were all recognized.

items.title: Watson III Tabbed For MAC Weekly Honor
items.summary: AMHERST, Mass. – Senior quarterback William "Pop" Watson III tabbed MAC Co-Offensive Player of the Week, as announced by the Mid-American Conference on Monday morning.

items.title: Minutemen Outlast Ball State in Overtime Thriller, 31-30
items.summary: The University of Massachusetts football team scored a touchdown in overtime, and converted the extra point, which was the difference in a hard-fought 31-30 overtime win over visiting Ball State on Wednesday night at McGuirk Alumni Stadium (8,881).

Dan and Diane Riccio Make $3 Million Commitment To The Script U Scholarship Society To Support UMass Football
items.summary: Daniel J. Riccio Jr. '86, '24MS and his wife, Diane M. (Casey) Riccio, Ph.D., have committed $3 million to the Script U Scholarship Society to support the University of Massachusetts Football program.

items.title: UMass football freefall continues at UConn
items.summary: EAST HARTFORD, Conn.  – The Massachusetts football team stacked up four wins to start the season like dominoes. Since then, those dominoes have fallen one by one, with the momentum of each loss falling into the next game. items.summary: EAST HARTFORD, Conn.— The Massachusetts football team traveled to Rentschler Field on Friday night, yet seemed to leave its offensive spark in Amherst, Mass., falling 35-16 to UConn.
